evidence.title: README (segment 3)
evidence.excerpt: This is a Java adapter to the [GitHub RESTful API]. There are a few other similar implementations on the market, but jcabi-github has a very strong focus on object-oriented principles of programming. On top of that, we have a unique implementation of GitHub server-side functionality, which you can use in your unit tests, eliminating the necessity to connect to GitHub during unit/integration testing. Please, read the blog post [_Object-Oriented GitHub API_][blog] by [Yegor Bugayenko](https://www.yegor256.com), the creator of this library.

evidence.title: README (segment 4)
evidence.excerpt: The set of classes in the [`com.jcabi.github`][package] package is the object-oriented API. Use it like this:

evidence.title: README (segment 5)
evidence.excerpt: ```java import com.jcabi.github.*; public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { GitHub github = new RtGitHub(".. your OAuth token .."); Repo repo = github.repos().get( new Coordinates.Simple("octocat/Hello-World") ); final Issue issue = repo.issues().create("Test title", "Test description"); issue.comments().post("My first comment!"); } } ```

evidence.title: README (segment 6)
evidence.excerpt: If you want to work with GitHub's API through another domain, you can use the URI-constructors of class `RtGitHub`. For instance, if you have your own instance of GitHub deployed under the domain `https://github.mydomain.com`, do the following:

evidence.title: README (segment 8)
evidence.excerpt: final GitHub github = new RtGitHub( "<<oauth2_token>>", URI.create("https://github.mydomain.com") );
